Mandatory Vaccinations - The Ethics and The Law

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The rights of the individual vs society

Unique Selling Point:
Globally there is a move towards shifting the burden of the pandemic on the unvaccinated, meaning that they will be excluded from certain sectors in order to minimise the burden on society at large. By excluding unvaccinated individuals from air travel, certain businesses like restaurants and group gatherings, and even some work situations, one lessens the risk of transmission, and the cost to the state and the individual in terms of testing and treatment. But can one force individuals to give up their personal rights for the greater good?

Summary:
"Mandatory Vaccinations" - a term that is more often used these days as the world scrambles to find ways of keeping people safe while returning to some form of normal. France and Italy have made vaccines mandatory for using indoor facilities like gyms, restaurants and other function venues. Kenya is making Covid vaccinations mandatory for all civil servants. San Francisco has made indoor events for the vaccinated only. CNN fired 3 employees for violating safety protocol and going to the office unvaccinated... The trend continues worldwide. South Africa is no exception. Sasol was one of the first employers to announce that Covid Vaccinations would be compulsory for its staff at the Secunda plant. The plant is set to enter an annual maintenance phase at the end of August and there is an estimated 19,000 people on site during this time. In order to avoid a super spreader event, Sasol decided everyone, including contractors would have to provide proof of vaccinations or a weekly PCR test to the person's own account. Needless to say there has been some pushback. People are adamant that mandatory vaccinations infringe on their personal rights, but how do we balance the right of the individual vs those of society.

Further information:
The world has been divided between US and THEM - the vaccinated and those who believe (for whatever reason) that the vaccine is a violation of their personal freedom.

While the SA Government has said on numerous occasions that no-one will be forced to get vaccinated against Covid-19, it does seem that it will be necessary to make vaccines mandatory for certain sectors. At the moment you need a yellow fever vaccine for travel to some countries and the same applies for Covid-19. In Britain home-based healthcare workers need to be vaccinated against Covid-19, and the same goes for many other countries and industries.

While people have the choice to go unvaccinated, their choice will mean they might need to give up on some societal benefits or even some fields of employment.

While there are plenty of moral reasons to get vaccinated, it doesn't necessarily mean it's your ethical duty, says Travis Rieder, from the Berman Institute of Bioethics at Johns Hopkins University. The straightforward ethical argument, is: Getting vaccinated isn’t just about you. Your freedom is limited by the harm it could do to others. In other words, you do not have the right to risk other people’s health, and so you are obligated to do your part to reduce infection and transmission rates.
Experts have said that in South Africa, employers do not have the right to demand a vaccination from an employee as it will be a direct violation of their basic human rights, and COSATU has also issued a stern warning to employers. The Department of Basic Education has alluded to the fact that vaccines would be mandatory for teachers. And in June Government said that employers do have the right to require proof of vaccination in some instances.

Some additional questions:
Do we have a duty to be vaccinated for the greater good?
Rights of the individual vs society's wellbeing
Rights of employees – whilst individuals have right to remain unvaccinated, others have the right to work in a safe environment. It can be argued that employers who allow unvaccinated staff to come to work, will be putting others at risk.
Should unvaccinated individuals be allowed to enjoy social privileges like going to the movies, restaurants and air travel?
As a teacher you should have the right to decide if you want a vaccine or not, but does the parent have a choice in whether or not their child is being taught by an unvaccinated teacher?
While doctors can probably not refuse to treat an unvaccinated patient, what about healthcare facilities like private hospitals? Or medical aids? Can a medical aid refuse someone membership on the grounds that they have not been vaccinated? And is it fair to expect a medical aid or even the state to cover the cost of your treatment if you chose not to be vaccinated?

Experts say that in order to effectively fight off the coronavirus we need large-scale global vaccines and at the moment it doesn't look like South Africa has that... vaccination sites across Gauteng is largely empty, or at least under utilised. How do we get people to vaccinate without making it law?

Press Release:


Vaccines: The Ethical Dilemma
When the pandemic hit, the world cried out for a vaccine. Within a year, medical experts produced a variety of COVID-19 vaccines which have shifted the outlook for COVID-19’s stranglehold on the globe – but only if a critical percentage choose to get jabbed. Are mandatory vaccinations the answer to get the world back to a pre-COVID norm, or do individuals who choose not to be vaccinated have a legal right to opt out? Globally, the move towards shifting the burden of the pandemic onto the unvaccinated is growing. But are we looking at a future wherein the unvaccinated will be marginalised? And how do we balance the freedom of individuals with the rights of society at large?
Producer: Stenette Grosskopf | Researcher: Laura Byrne | Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli

Script:


VACCINE ETHICS MASTER Script
UPSOUND
Free Covid-19 Vaccine. Everyone, everyone is allowed...
V/O
Since the South African Covid-19 vaccine roll out began earlier this year about 12 million jabs have been administered… but the uptake hasn’t been enthusiastic across the board.
UPSOUND
Sorreey, luvvie.

LINK:
Mandatory Vaccines, that’s what people are talking about. And the world is moving towards a no-jab-no-entry policy… restaurants, in-door venues… even air travel is fast becoming only for the vaccinated...
V/O
But mandatory vaccinations are being met with resistance. Anti-vaxx protests have been staged across the globe, from Australia, Asia and the US to Europe… and South Africa is no exception...
UPSOUND SA PROTEST
“No to the jab!”
V/O
To date only about 9% of the South African population has been fully vaccinated, but Wits Professor of Vaccinology, Shabir Madhi, believes this is not necessarily a true reflection of people’s sentiment on vaccines...
Shabir Madhi
I don't believe there's a huge amount of vaccine hesitancy in South Africa. In fact, the low coverage that we've got is more a function of access to vaccines rather than a large number of people being hesitant to be vaccinated.
V/O
Mistakes and delays during the vaccine rollout have impacted the numbers…

The anti-vaxx noise, he believes, comes from a very vocal few...
Shabir Madhi
There's a small minority of individuals that are for some reason, and it really defies my understanding what their true motive is. They strongly believe that vaccines are to harm them. Never in the history of humanity, if we develop vaccines to harm individuals, our vaccines have always been developed to save lives.
V/O
Anti-Vaxx conspiracies are born from the mistrust of authority and government, says lecturer in critical thinking and ethics at the University of Cape Town, Jacques Rousseau...
Jacques Rousseau
In any situation of moral panic, in a sense, where we think that there's potentially an existential threat to civilization, we are going to see a rise in that sort of thing. And it's not helped by the fact that prominent doctors are spreading anti vaccine tropes on social media…
V/O
But questioning vaccines is not just the realm of conspiracy theorists… Some people are simply concerned about their health, doubting the efficacy of vaccines developed in record time....
Shabir Madhi
But there's a reason we needed to take ten and a half months and not ten and a half years, because had we taken 10 and a half years, the number of people that would have ended up dying from COVID 19 would be probably eventually five times higher than what would be the case now that we do have vaccines available.
V/O
The severe impact on our healthcare systems across the world coupled with the economic disruptions caused by lockdowns, means that Vaccines are pushed to the fore by Government and the private sector in an effort to return the world to what we knew as “normal”.
LINK
In a drive to get more people vaccinated the Gauteng Department of Health has decided to put up pop-up centres like this one all over the province.
V/O
The list of international compulsory vaccine requirements is growing … Healthcare workers and public servants in many countries are now required to get the jab. Cities like New York, San Francisco and Paris are demanding proof of vaccination for entry into most public buildings, and fines for those who do not comply. In South Africa the rules have not been set... yet.
Jacques Rousseau
I think we have to go the same route, and I understand people's objections. I do understand because this is clearly a violation of personal liberty. But what people don't understand about freedom and about the rules that we use to govern our freedoms is that they serve a purpose. They serve a purpose of making everybody maximally free overall. So a violation of my or your liberty, forcing me to get a vaccine is a violation, but it's a tiny violation in respect of the benefits that it can purchase for the entirety of society.
V/O
For Rousseau it is clear that we all have an ethical obligation to be vaccinated.
VOXPOPS
“I buried my father last week from Covid-19 pneumonia. So for my family it’s a huge thing because actually the day of his memorial was the day that he was meant to get his jab....”
V/O
A Covid-19 vaccine means that you are 50 to 80% less likely to get the virus, and if you get sick, the probability of passing it on to someone else is reduced by 50%. But where the vaccines are extremely effective, is in preventing severe disease, hospitalisation and death. Official Government Reports say that we have lost around 81,000 people due to Covid-19 thus far, but Madhi says that’s clearly not the case.
Shabir Madhi
South Africa is amongst the top five countries with the highest number of people that have died of COVID 19 per capita. The number of people that have died in South Africa from COVID 19 is closer to 230 to 240000 based on excess mortality data.
V/O
And part of the problem is that Government is downplaying the numbers, which means that the citizens do not understand the sense of urgency…

And even though this generation of vaccines will not rid us of SARS-CoV-2, there is a public health imperative to vaccinate as many people as possible, says Madhi. But is mandatory vaccinations the way forward?
Shabir Madhi
We cannot talk about mandatory vaccination unless it's adequate access to vaccines to all of this is contingent on the state ensuring that there's adequate supply of vaccine that is accessible.
V/O
Millions of undocumented individuals currently have no access to these vaccines… although the Department has indicated that this will be addressed from October…
Shabir Madhi
I think it would be difficult to legislate mandatory vaccination in any country, for that matter. But there can be restrictions placed upon people that choose not to be vaccinated, and those sort of restrictions are fully justified.
V/O
Similar to what is happening in Europe and other countries, unvaccinated people will be refused entry to some restaurants, indoor venues and events… but this will likely be largely driven by the private sector, says Madhi...
Jacques Rousseau
Mac: But is it fair, though, because for me, in some way, it seems a little bit discriminatory to say you have to get it or you can't get into this particular place?

Well, it's unfair and unfair is one of those things that people sometimes view as the eye of the beholder sort of thing. I would rather say it's unfair for people who might be carrying a contagion to think that they have the right to engage in public activities and put me and everybody else at risk.
Neil Searle
The things that's important to bear in mind as a starting point is there is no general law that requires citizens to be vaccinated in South Africa. And that's why this has been such a such a moving target and such a challenging concept for for everybody.
V/O
On Friday the Department announced that mandatory vaccines might be needed for certain sectors, but it has not confirmed any details yet...

Meanwhile, businesses have been armed for the inevitable, says Neil Searle -- specialist Labour litigator at the corporate law firm, Fasken.
Neil Searle
Mac: So, Neil can a South African company make it mandatory for its staff to get, you know, COVID 19 vaccines.

So the short answer, McFarlan, is yes, they can. The Department of Labor published its consolidated directions that now require an employer, all employers with more than 10 employees, to conduct a risk assessment to determine whether or not to implement a mandatory vaccination policy in their workplace.
LINK:
Chemical and Energy giant, Sasol made headlines recently when it was reported that all workers at the Secunda plant would need Covid-19 vaccines for the duration of the maintenance period...
V/O
Dr Hilko Johannsmeier heads up the Health Department at Sasol, and says about 18,000 people migrate to the work environment during the annual Secunda shut-down in September.
Dr Johannsmeier
And this is obviously posing an additional risk to our normal operations. And we’ve done a thorough revision of our Covid-19 risk assessment and it basically established that we may be sitting on a potential super-spreader...
V/O
For this reason, Covid-19 vaccinations will be a requirement for this specific maintenance event in Secunda, but contrary to initial media reports, Sasol is accommodating unvaccinated workers.
Dr Johannsmeier
Individuals who do not want to be vaccinated or have a contraindication to vaccinations then have an alternative to be frequently tested to enter the workplace, so that we can still maintain a safe working environment as far as possible...
V/O
Even with the Government’s guidelines, employers may very well face complications, says Searle, as ‘compulsory vaccines in the workplace’ is largely uncharted territory...
Neil Searle
I think you're going to find, as we sort of seeing already, employers approaching these issues with with with a lot of caution. You're obviously walking somewhat of a of a legal minefield in terms of the procedural requirements and the legal risks that arise … So it's it's really, I think, in circumstances where there is a high risk of transmission in the workplace and where those workplaces and work systems can't be adapted to limit the risk of transmission, that you're going to find that those employers are the ones who ultimately decide to implement mandatory vaccination policies.
V/O
A system of incentives and disincentives might prove to be more effective than blanket compulsory vaccination policies.
Jacques Rousseau
We want to try to get people to do this out of their own free will, not only because it avoids coercion, but also because it avoids that mistrust of authority and in a sense, a dictatorial style imposition on us as free individuals.
V/O
We’re already seeing businesses motivating people to vaccinate against Covid-19. Retailers are offering discounts to the vaccinated, medical aids are offering special deals for jabbed members… even restaurants are joining the trend…

For now, it seems, until most people accept Covid-19 vaccines as the new normal, the world is shifting the burden of the pandemic to the unvaccinated...
Shabir Madhi
I think we need to start thinking, yes, people should have a choice of not being vaccinated, but that every choice that you're making, life comes with consequences and it shouldn't be any different for people who choose not to be vaccinated...



Promo 1 11”
Are mandatory vaccine policies ethical, and even legal? And if you decline the jab, should you be accommodated at work and still enjoy society’s benefits? Experts answer some burning questions...


Promo 2 21”
In a race against time the world has developed much-needed Covid-19 vaccines, but while we need to vaccinate as many people as possible, some question the jab and have been vocal about their distrust...

UPSOUND Never in the history of humanity have we developed vaccines to harm individuals, our vaccines have always been developed to save lives.

Is it our moral duty to be vaccinated?


Promo 3 21”
Since March 2020 South Africans have been suffering because of Covid-19.

UPSOUND: South Africa is amongst the top five countries with the highest number of people that have died of COVID 19 per capita.

At the moment vaccines are the only way to tame the wave and reduce the number of mortalities, but should we resort to mandatory vaccinations?

Jacques Rousseau In any situation of moral panic, in a sense, where we think that there's potentially an existential threat to civilization, we are going to see a rise in that sort of thing. And it's not helped by the fact that prominent doctors are spreading anti vaccine tropes on social media… V/O But questioning vaccines is not just the realm of conspiracy theorists… Some people are simply concerned about their health, doubting the efficacy of vaccines developed in record time.... Shabir Madhi But there's a reason we needed to take ten and a half months and not ten and a half years, because had we taken 10 and a half years, the number of people that would have ended up dying from COVID 19 would be probably eventually five times higher than what would be the case now that we do have vaccines available. V/O The severe impact on our healthcare systems across the world coupled with the economic disruptions caused by lockdowns, means that Vaccines are pushed to the fore by Government and the private sector in an effort to return the world to what we knew as “normal”. LINK In a drive to get more people vaccinated the Gauteng Department of Health has decided to put up pop-up centres like this one all over the province. V/O The list of international compulsory vaccine requirements is growing … Healthcare workers and public servants in many countries are now required to get the jab. Cities like New York, San Francisco and Paris are demanding proof of vaccination for entry into most public buildings, and fines for those who do not comply. In South Africa the rules have not been set... yet. Jacques Rousseau I think we have to go the same route, and I understand people's objections. I do understand because this is clearly a violation of personal liberty. But what people don't understand about freedom and about the rules that we use to govern our freedoms is that they serve a purpose. They serve a purpose of making everybody maximally free overall. So a violation of my or your liberty, forcing me to get a vaccine is a violation, but it's a tiny violation in respect of the benefits that it can purchase for the entirety of society. V/O For Rousseau it is clear that we all have an ethical obligation to be vaccinated. VOXPOPS “I buried my father last week from Covid-19 pneumonia. So for my family it’s a huge thing because actually the day of his memorial was the day that he was meant to get his jab....” V/O A Covid-19 vaccine means that you are 50 to 80% less likely to get the virus, and if you get sick, the probability of passing it on to someone else is reduced by 50%. But where the vaccines are extremely effective, is in preventing severe disease, hospitalisation and death. Official Government Reports say that we have lost around 81,000 people due to Covid-19 thus far, but Madhi says that’s clearly not the case. Shabir Madhi South Africa is amongst the top five countries with the highest number of people that have died of COVID 19 per capita. The number of people that have died in South Africa from COVID 19 is closer to 230 to 240000 based on excess mortality data. V/O And part of the problem is that Government is downplaying the numbers, which means that the citizens do not understand the sense of urgency… And even though this generation of vaccines will not rid us of SARS-CoV-2, there is a public health imperative to vaccinate as many people as possible, says Madhi. But is mandatory vaccinations the way forward? Shabir Madhi We cannot talk about mandatory vaccination unless it's adequate access to vaccines to all of this is contingent on the state ensuring that there's adequate supply of vaccine that is accessible. V/O Millions of undocumented individuals currently have no access to these vaccines… although the Department has indicated that this will be addressed from October… Shabir Madhi I think it would be difficult to legislate mandatory vaccination in any country, for that matter. But there can be restrictions placed upon people that choose not to be vaccinated, and those sort of restrictions are fully justified. V/O Similar to what is happening in Europe and other countries, unvaccinated people will be refused entry to some restaurants, indoor venues and events… but this will likely be largely driven by the private sector, says Madhi... Jacques Rousseau Mac: But is it fair, though, because for me, in some way, it seems a little bit discriminatory to say you have to get it or you can't get into this particular place? Well, it's unfair and unfair is one of those things that people sometimes view as the eye of the beholder sort of thing. I would rather say it's unfair for people who might be carrying a contagion to think that they have the right to engage in public activities and put me and everybody else at risk. Neil Searle The things that's important to bear in mind as a starting point is there is no general law that requires citizens to be vaccinated in South Africa. And that's why this has been such a such a moving target and such a challenging concept for for everybody. V/O On Friday the Department announced that mandatory vaccines might be needed for certain sectors, but it has not confirmed any details yet... Meanwhile, businesses have been armed for the inevitable, says Neil Searle -- specialist Labour litigator at the corporate law firm, Fasken. Neil Searle Mac: So, Neil can a South African company make it mandatory for its staff to get, you know, COVID 19 vaccines. So the short answer, McFarlan, is yes, they can. The Department of Labor published its consolidated directions that now require an employer, all employers with more than 10 employees, to conduct a risk assessment to determine whether or not to implement a mandatory vaccination policy in their workplace. LINK: Chemical and Energy giant, Sasol made headlines recently when it was reported that all workers at the Secunda plant would need Covid-19 vaccines for the duration of the maintenance period... V/O Dr Hilko Johannsmeier heads up the Health Department at Sasol, and says about 18,000 people migrate to the work environment during the annual Secunda shut-down in September. Dr Johannsmeier And this is obviously posing an additional risk to our normal operations. And we’ve done a thorough revision of our Covid-19 risk assessment and it basically established that we may be sitting on a potential super-spreader... V/O For this reason, Covid-19 vaccinations will be a requirement for this specific maintenance event in Secunda, but contrary to initial media reports, Sasol is accommodating unvaccinated workers. Dr Johannsmeier Individuals who do not want to be vaccinated or have a contraindication to vaccinations then have an alternative to be frequently tested to enter the workplace, so that we can still maintain a safe working environment as far as possible... V/O Even with the Government’s guidelines, employers may very well face complications, says Searle, as ‘compulsory vaccines in the workplace’ is largely uncharted territory... Neil Searle I think you're going to find, as we sort of seeing already, employers approaching these issues with with with a lot of caution. You're obviously walking somewhat of a of a legal minefield in terms of the procedural requirements and the legal risks that arise … So it's it's really, I think, in circumstances where there is a high risk of transmission in the workplace and where those workplaces and work systems can't be adapted to limit the risk of transmission, that you're going to find that those employers are the ones who ultimately decide to implement mandatory vaccination policies. V/O A system of incentives and disincentives might prove to be more effective than blanket compulsory vaccination policies. Jacques Rousseau We want to try to get people to do this out of their own free will, not only because it avoids coercion, but also because it avoids that mistrust of authority and in a sense, a dictatorial style imposition on us as free individuals. V/O We’re already seeing businesses motivating people to vaccinate against Covid-19. Retailers are offering discounts to the vaccinated, medical aids are offering special deals for jabbed members… even restaurants are joining the trend… For now, it seems, until most people accept Covid-19 vaccines as the new normal, the world is shifting the burden of the pandemic to the unvaccinated... Shabir Madhi I think we need to start thinking, yes, people should have a choice of not being vaccinated, but that every choice that you're making, life comes with consequences and it shouldn't be any different for people who choose not to be vaccinated... Promo 1 11” Are mandatory vaccine policies ethical, and even legal? And if you decline the jab, should you be accommodated at work and still enjoy society’s benefits? Experts answer some burning questions... Promo 2 21” In a race against time the world has developed much-needed Covid-19 vaccines, but while we need to vaccinate as many people as possible, some question the jab and have been vocal about their distrust... UPSOUND Never in the history of humanity have we developed vaccines to harm individuals, our vaccines have always been developed to save lives. Is it our moral duty to be vaccinated? Promo 3 21” Since March 2020 South Africans have been suffering because of Covid-19. UPSOUND: South Africa is amongst the top five countries with the highest number of people that have died of COVID 19 per capita. At the moment vaccines are the only way to tame the wave and reduce the number of mortalities, but should we resort to mandatory vaccinations?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The rights of the individual vs society
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Globally there is a move towards shifting the burden of the pandemic on the unvaccinated, meaning that they will be excluded from certain sectors in order to minimise the burden on society at large. By excluding unvaccinated individuals from air travel, certain businesses like restaurants and group gatherings, and even some work situations, one lessens the risk of transmission, and the cost to the state and the individual in terms of testing and treatment. But can one force individuals to give up their personal rights for the greater good?
metadata.Summary: "Mandatory Vaccinations" - a term that is more often used these days as the world scrambles to find ways of keeping people safe while returning to some form of normal. France and Italy have made vaccines mandatory for using indoor facilities like gyms, restaurants and other function venues. Kenya is making Covid vaccinations mandatory for all civil servants. San Francisco has made indoor events for the vaccinated only. CNN fired 3 employees for violating safety protocol and going to the office unvaccinated... The trend continues worldwide. South Africa is no exception. Sasol was one of the first employers to announce that Covid Vaccinations would be compulsory for its staff at the Secunda plant. The plant is set to enter an annual maintenance phase at the end of August and there is an estimated 19,000 people on site during this time. In order to avoid a super spreader event, Sasol decided everyone, including contractors would have to provide proof of vaccinations or a weekly PCR test to the person's own account. Needless to say there has been some pushback. People are adamant that mandatory vaccinations infringe on their personal rights, but how do we balance the right of the individual vs those of society.
metadata.Further information: The world has been divided between US and THEM - the vaccinated and those who believe (for whatever reason) that the vaccine is a violation of their personal freedom. While the SA Government has said on numerous occasions that no-one will be forced to get vaccinated against Covid-19, it does seem that it will be necessary to make vaccines mandatory for certain sectors. At the moment you need a yellow fever vaccine for travel to some countries and the same applies for Covid-19. In Britain home-based healthcare workers need to be vaccinated against Covid-19, and the same goes for many other countries and industries. While people have the choice to go unvaccinated, their choice will mean they might need to give up on some societal benefits or even some fields of employment. While there are plenty of moral reasons to get vaccinated, it doesn't necessarily mean it's your ethical duty, says Travis Rieder, from the Berman Institute of Bioethics at Johns Hopkins University. The straightforward ethical argument, is: Getting vaccinated isn’t just about you. Your freedom is limited by the harm it could do to others. In other words, you do not have the right to risk other people’s health, and so you are obligated to do your part to reduce infection and transmission rates. Experts have said that in South Africa, employers do not have the right to demand a vaccination from an employee as it will be a direct violation of their basic human rights, and COSATU has also issued a stern warning to employers. The Department of Basic Education has alluded to the fact that vaccines would be mandatory for teachers. And in June Government said that employers do have the right to require proof of vaccination in some instances. Some additional questions: Do we have a duty to be vaccinated for the greater good? Rights of the individual vs society's wellbeing Rights of employees – whilst individuals have right to remain unvaccinated, others have the right to work in a safe environment. It can be argued that employers who allow unvaccinated staff to come to work, will be putting others at risk. Should unvaccinated individuals be allowed to enjoy social privileges like going to the movies, restaurants and air travel? As a teacher you should have the right to decide if you want a vaccine or not, but does the parent have a choice in whether or not their child is being taught by an unvaccinated teacher? While doctors can probably not refuse to treat an unvaccinated patient, what about healthcare facilities like private hospitals? Or medical aids? Can a medical aid refuse someone membership on the grounds that they have not been vaccinated? And is it fair to expect a medical aid or even the state to cover the cost of your treatment if you chose not to be vaccinated? Experts say that in order to effectively fight off the coronavirus we need large-scale global vaccines and at the moment it doesn't look like South Africa has that... vaccination sites across Gauteng is largely empty, or at least under utilised. How do we get people to vaccinate without making it law?
